mechanism_narrative: If WORKPLACES rebounds after the sharp t-1w drop, weekday foot traffic returns first, then retail-and-recreation spending follows with a short lag, lifting RETAIL_REC over the next four weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:WORKPLACES fell to -32.6 at t-1w and then recovered to -6.4 at t-0w
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC stays below the last 4-week mean while WORKPLACES continues to recover for four straight weeks.

mechanism_narrative: When RESIDENTIAL stays elevated above its recent norm, households shift spending toward nearby retail and recreation venues after time at home, pushing RETAIL_REC higher within one week.
candidate_trigger: RESIDENTIAL remains at least 3 points above the prior week's level
evidence_refs: fact:RESIDENTIAL was 10.9 at t-1w and 6.7 at t-0w after a 7.3 to 6.7 range
failure_condition: A week with RESIDENTIAL above the prior week by at least 3 points is followed by no increase in RETAIL_REC within 7 days.

mechanism_narrative: A joint rise in TRANSIT and WORKPLACES increases accessible daytime demand for shopping and leisure trips, so RETAIL_REC rises over the next two to four weeks when both series move upward together.
evidence_refs: fact:TRANSIT improved from -15.1 to -10.6 while WORKPLACES recovered from -32.6 to -6.4 at t-0w
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not rise over the next 14 days when TRANSIT and WORKPLACES both increase from their prior-week levels.

mechanism_narrative: If PARKS jumps while GROCERY_PHARM remains elevated, households are reallocating time toward non-retail outdoor activity and essentials, which suppresses discretionary retail visits and lowers RETAIL_REC over four weeks.
candidate_trigger: PARKS rises above -10 while GROCERY_PHARM stays above 25
evidence_refs: fact:PARKS rose to -4.6 at t-1w while GROCERY_PHARM stayed high at 34.6
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC increases over the next 28 days despite PARKS staying above -10 and GROCERY_PHARM staying above 25.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in GROCERY_PHARM signals fewer precautionary trips and less errand clustering, which releases spending back into retail and recreation with a one to two week lag, raising RETAIL_REC.
candidate_trigger: GROCERY_PHARM falls by 5 points or more from the previous week
evidence_refs: fact:GROCERY_PHARM dropped from 34.6 at t-1w to 28.0 at t-0w
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC fails to improve within 14 days after a weekly decline of at least 5 points in GROCERY_PHARM.

mechanism_narrative: In a tighter-restriction regime, the combination of falling TRANSIT and flat-to-falling WORKPLACES reduces discretionary out-of-home activity, so RETAIL_REC declines over the next four weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:TRANSIT was negative in all four weeks and WORKPLACES remained below baseline overall
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC rises above its last-4-week mean while TRANSIT and WORKPLACES both remain below baseline for the entire next month.

mechanism_narrative: A one-week jump in PARKS draws leisure time away from malls, restaurants, and shopping districts, so retail-and-recreation mobility weakens immediately and stays softer over the following week.
candidate_trigger: PARKS increases by at least 8 points week-on-week
evidence_refs: fact:PARKS moved from -14.9 at t-2w to -4.6 at t-1w before dropping again
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not decline within 7 days after PARKS rises by at least 8 points in a week.

mechanism_narrative: When TRANSIT improves but RESIDENTIAL also stays high, the extra commuting and home-based demand coexist, creating more mixed-purpose trips that support retail visits over the next two weeks.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT rises while RESIDENTIAL stays at or above 6
evidence_refs: fact:TRANSIT improved to -10.6 at t-0w while RESIDENTIAL remained 6.7
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not increase within 14 days when TRANSIT rises and RESIDENTIAL remains at or above 6.
